# Joggins Fossil Cliffs · UNESCO World Heritage Site

![Joggins Fossil Cliffs at golden hour](https://jogginsfossilcliffs.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/hero_06.jpg)

## Rock. Solid. History.

![Joggins Fossil Cliffs at golden hour, low tide](https://jogginsfossilcliffs.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/hero_01.jpg)

![fossil at Joggins](https://jogginsfossilcliffs.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/hero_12.jpg)

![Beach at Joggins, Nova Scotia, with cliffs in foreground](https://jogginsfossilcliffs.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/hero_22.jpg)

## The Joggins Fossil Centre is closed for the winter, and will reopen on May 1, 2027

Access to the Joggins Fossil Cliffs (beach) remains open for the time being.

Please be mindful of [tides](https://jogginsfossilcliffs.net/2026/06/tide-schedule-and-suggested-beach-times/) and [safety](https://jogginsfossilcliffs.net/tours/safety/).

![Joggins Fossil Cliffs on a sunny day](https://jogginsfossilcliffs.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/011.jpg)

Where the world-famous Bay of Fundy exposes a 300-million-year-old story.

Preserved in nature, uncovered by force. Explore one of nature’s most inspiring creations, where the highest tides in the world reveal the most complete fossil record of the _Coal Age,_ 100 million years before the dinosaurs. Every rock holds the possibility of discovery, and our guided tours may lead you to finding a missing piece of time’s puzzle. At Joggins, our backyard may be 300 million years old but every day is different!

## The Joggins Fossil Centre

The Joggins Fossil Centre is situated on the reclaimed site of the Old Joggins No. 7 Coal Mine overlooking the Joggins Fossil Cliffs. The Centre provides an exceptional learning experience, featuring an extensive fossil specimen collection, exhibits, and displays depicting:

- The rich geological history of the Joggins Cliffs


- The history of scientific discovery at the Joggins Fossil Cliffs


- How the history of coal mining shaped the local community.



## Season and hours

- **Open: May 1 to October 18**, 2026 — 10 am to 5 pm

- **Closed: September 30** (Truth and Reconciliation day) and

- **Closed: October 12** (Thanksgiving)

## Roofed accommodations

Structure ready to shelter, no assembly required.

[![A father and son eating s’mores at an oTENTik in Cheticamp Campground.](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/voyage-travel/hebergement-accommodation/thumbs/02-NS-CBH-2015-27-335x227.jpg)**oTENTik**](https://parks.canada.ca/voyage-travel/hebergement-accommodation/otentik)

A small house-like shelter with sleeping platforms, furniture, and heating.

[![A yurt deck provides plenty of space to relax in deck chairs, cook or keep warm by the fire.](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/voyage-travel/hebergement-accommodation/yourte-yurt-alt-355.jpg)**Yurt**](https://parks.canada.ca/voyage-travel/hebergement-accommodation/yourte-yurt)

A round hut with beds, furniture and heating.

[![Two visitors gaze at the Big Dipper outside a tipi on a starry night.](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/voyage-travel/hebergement-accommodation/thumbs/09-AB-RMH-2016-084-335x227.jpg)**Tipi**](https://parks.canada.ca/voyage-travel/hebergement-accommodation/tipi)

Traditional canvas shelter with wood floor, table, chairs and sleeping mats.
